atoms.name: Addresses, classes, reserved
atoms.one_line: 32-bit address; class from first octet; network and broadcast addresses are not assignable, so hosts = 2^h - 2.

atoms.name: CIDR prefix and mask
atoms.one_line: /n means n leading ones; the partial octet is 128, 192, 224, 240, 248, 252, 254 and its block size is 256 minus that.

atoms.name: Network address and same subnet
atoms.one_line: AND with the mask (or round down to the block); equal results mean the same subnet.

atoms.name: Subnetting and VLSM
atoms.one_line: Borrow bits for subnets; hosts per subnet 2^h - 2; every LAN and every router link is a subnet.

atoms.name: Supernetting and aggregation
atoms.one_line: A block starts at a multiple of its size; merge aligned blocks; smallest covering prefix must contain both ends.

atoms.name: Longest-prefix match
atoms.one_line: Collect every matching prefix and take the longest; default is /0; row order is irrelevant.

atoms.name: Header fields
atoms.one_line: HLEN counts 4-byte words; TTL and checksum change at each hop; payload is total length minus header.

atoms.name: Fragmentation
atoms.one_line: Data per fragment = (MTU - header) rounded down to 8; offset is start over 8; MF is 0 only on the last fragment.

atoms.name: Multi-MTU fragmentation and reassembly
atoms.one_line: Each router re-splits the pieces it gets; only the destination reassembles; total payload is last offset times 8 plus its data.

atoms.name: NAT basics
atoms.one_line: Private ranges 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16; NAT rewrites source IP and port outbound, destination inbound, and the checksums.

atoms.name: IP versus MAC per hop
atoms.one_line: Destination IP is end to end; MAC addresses are rewritten at each link, and the first MAC is the next-hop router.
